questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Moses would happen after Israel punished the Midianites?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses that after that, Moses would die and be with his ancestors who had already died.

questions.q: How many soldiers was each tribe to send to war against Midian?
questions.a: Each tribe was to send a thousand soldiers.

questions.q: What happened in Israel’s battle against Midian?
questions.a: All the Midianite men were killed, including their kings and Balaam.

questions.q: What did the Israelites take as plunder from Midian?
questions.a: The Israelites took the women of Midian, their children, and all their farm animals and valuable things that belonged to them as plunder.

questions.q: What did the Israelites do to the cities and encampments where the Midianites lived?
questions.a: They burned them all with fire.

questions.q: Where did the Israelites bring everything that they had captured after the battle?
questions.a: They brought everything they had captured to the camp to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the congregation of the Israelites, in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan River at Jericho.

questions.q: Why was Moses angry with the commanders of the army of Israel?
questions.a: Moses was angry with the commanders because they had let all the women of Midian live.

questions.q: Why was Moses angry that the officers of the army of Israel had let the women of Midian live?
questions.a: Moses was angry because the women of Midian had caused the Israelites, through Balaam’s advice, to stop being loyal to Yahweh.

questions.q: Who did Moses command the commanders of the army of Israel to kill?
questions.a: Moses told the commanders to kill every male among the children and every woman who had slept with a man.

questions.q: How long did the soldiers who had killed anyone or touched a dead body have to camp outside the camp of Israel?
questions.a: They were to stay outside the camp for seven days.

questions.q: Who did Moses tell the commanders of the army they must allow to live among them?
questions.a: Moses told the commanders of the army that they must allow all the young girls who had never slept with a man to live among them.

questions.q: How long were those who had killed a person or touched a corpse to camp outside of the camp?
questions.a: They were to camp outside of the camp for seven days.

questions.q: What were the Israelites to purify?
questions.a: They were to purify every piece of clothing and every item that people made out of animal skin, goat hair, or wood.

questions.q: What did Eleazar the priest say to do with the gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, lead, and everything that could go through the fire?
questions.a: He said to make everything that could go through the fire go through the fire, and it would be clean, but it must also be purified with the water of impurity.

questions.q: What did the soldiers have to do before they could return to the camp?
questions.a: They had to wash their clothes on the seventh day. Then they would be clean and could return to the camp.

questions.q: Between what two groups did Yahweh tell Moses to divide the plunder from the war?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses to divide the plunder between the soldiers who went out to battle and the rest of the congregation of Israel.

questions.q: What was the levy that the soldiers were to pay to Eleazar the priest?
questions.a: The soldiers were to pay a levy of one out of every 500 persons, cattle, donkeys, sheep, or goats.

questions.q: What was the levy the Israelites were to give to the Levites who took care of the tabernacle?
questions.a: The Israelites were to pay a levy of one out of every 50 persons, cattle, donkeys, sheep, and goats.

questions.q: How many sheep and goats, cattle, donkeys, and women did the Israelites capture from Midian in all?
questions.a: They captured 675,000 sheep and goats, 72,000 cattle, 61,000 donkeys, and 32,000 women who had not slept with a man.

questions.q: What portion of the plunder did the soldiers who fought receive, and what did they give to Yahweh from it?
questions.a: The soldiers received half of everything captured: 337,500 sheep and goats, 36,000 cattle, 30,500 donkeys, and 16,000 people. From that half, they gave Yahweh a tax of 675 sheep and goats, 72 cattle, 61 donkeys, and 32 people.

questions.q: What did Moses do with the levy that was set apart for Yahweh?
questions.a: Moses gave it to Eleazar the priest, just as Yahweh had commanded him.

questions.q: What portion of the plunder did the rest of the Israelite community receive?
questions.a: They received the other half: 337,500 sheep and goats, 36,000 cattle, 30,500 donkeys, and 16,000 people.

questions.q: What did Moses give to the Levites from the community’s half of the plunder?
questions.a: He gave them one out of every 50 people and animals, because the Levites took care of the tabernacle.

questions.q: What did the army commanders tell Moses when they came to him?
questions.a: They told him that they had counted the soldiers under their command and that none were missing.

questions.q: Why did the commanders of the army of Israel bring Yahweh offerings?
questions.a: They brought the offerings to make atonement for themselves before Yahweh.

questions.q: Why was all the gold from the army commanders given over to Yahweh?
questions.a: It was placed in the tent of meeting to remind Yahweh of the people of Israel.

commentary.text: Verses 1–6 All who, without commission from God, dare to execute private revenge, and who, from ambition, covetousness, or resentment, wage war and desolate kingdoms, must one day answer for it. But if God, instead of sending an earthquake, a pestilence, or a famine, be pleased to authorize and command any people to avenge his cause, such a commission surely is just and right. The Israelites could show such a commission, though no persons now can do so. Their wars were begun and carried on expressly by Divine direction, and they were enabled to conquer by miracles. Unless it can be proved that the wicked Canaanites did not deserve their doom, objectors only prove their dislike to God, and their love to his enemies. Man makes light of the evil of sin, but God abhors it. This explains the terrible executions of the nations which had filled the measure of their sins.

The Israelites slew the Kings of Midian. They slew Balaam. God's overruling providence brought him thither, and their just vengeance found him. Had he himself rightly believed what he had said of the happy state of Israel, he would not have thus herded with the enemies of Israel. The Midianites' wicked wiles were Balaam's projects: it was just that he should perish with them, Ho 4:5. They took the women and children captives. They burnt their cities and castles, and returned to the camp.

The sword of war should spare women and children; but the sword of justice should know no distinction, but that of guilty or not guilty. This war was the execution of a righteous sentence upon a guilty nation, in which the women were the worst criminals. The female children were spared, who, being brought up among the Israelites, would not tempt them to idolatry. The whole history shows the hatefulness of sin, and the guilt of tempting others; it teaches us to avoid all occasions of evil, and to give no quarter to inward lusts. The women and children were not kept for sinful purposes, but for slaves, a custom every where practised in former times, as to captives. In the course of providence, when famine and plagues visit a nation for sin, children suffer in the common calamity. In this case parents are punished in their children; and for children dying before actual sin, full provision is made as to their eternal happiness, by the mercy of God in Christ.

The Israelites had to purify themselves according to the law, and to abide without the camp seven days, though they had not contracted any moral guilt, the war being just and lawful, and commanded by God. Thus God would preserve in their minds a dread and detestation of shedding blood. The spoil had been used by Midianites, and being now come into the possession of Israelites, it was fit that it should be purified.

Whatever we have, God justly claims a part. Out of the people's share God required one in fifty, but out of the soldiers' share only one in five hundred. The less opportunity we have of honouring God with personal services, the more should we give in money or value.

The success of the Israelites had been very remarkable, so small a company overcoming such multitudes, but it was still more wonderful that not one was slain or missing. They presented the gold they found among the spoils, as an offering to the Lord. Thus they confessed, that instead of claiming a reward for their service, they needed forgiveness of much that had been amiss, and desired to be thankful for the preservation of their lives, which might justly have been taken away.
